author: Robert Carr
description: Lightly seared chicken and broccoli in an orange, ginger, garlic, and toasted-sesame sauce, served with brown rice.
equipment: 12-inch stainless steel skillet with a lid, such as All-Clad D5; a nonstick skillet also works
Rice cooker, such as Zojirushi NP-HCC10/XH, or a saucepan with a tight-fitting lid
Small bowl and whisk for sauce
Measuring cups and spoons; fine grater
Knife and separate cutting boards for produce and raw chicken
Shallow refrigerator- and freezer-safe containers, for meal prep

groceryIngredients.note: Plain, unbrined chicken without added salt solution; about 680 g.
Plain dry rice; a standard US measuring cup, about 180 g.
About 454 g; 1 1/2-inch florets with thick stems sliced thinly.
Medium sweet oranges, for 1/2 cup juice and 2 tsp finely grated zest. Measure the yield.
Reduced-sodium, about 590 mg sodium per tablespoon; check the label, not regular soy sauce.
Unseasoned; not sweetened seasoned rice vinegar.
For two batches of chicken and the aromatics.
For finishing; not the chicken searing oil.
Thinly sliced; keep white/light-green parts separate from dark-green tops.

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, plain and unbrined, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup dry brown basmati rice, about 180 g; use a standard US measuring cup
1 3/4 cups water for rice, or the amount on its package, plus 1/4 cup for broccoli, 1/4 cup for sauce, and small amounts as needed
1 lb (454 g) broccoli florets, about 1 1/2 inches wide, with thick stems sliced thinly
2 medium sweet oranges, for 1/2 cup fresh juice and 2 teaspoons finely grated zest
4 teaspoons cornstarch, divided: 2 teaspoons chicken and 2 teaspoons sauce
1 1/2 tablespoons canola oil, divided: 2 teaspoons per chicken batch and 1/2 teaspoon aromatics
3 green onions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
instructions: Choose the rice-cooker option in the notes or this saucepan method, not both; start the rice first and prepare the other ingredients while it cooks. For the saucepan, rinse and drain the rice, combine with 1 3/4 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for about 40 minutes. Remove from heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Follow the package ratio and timing when different; no oil or salt is needed. If still firm and dry, add 1 to 2 tablespoons water and cook covered a little longer.

Wash and prepare produce before handling raw chicken. Grate 2 teaspoons orange zest without the white pith, then squeeze and measure 1/2 cup juice. Whisk the juice, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, 1/4 cup water, 2 teaspoons cornstarch, and optional red pepper in a clean bowl. Keep the zest, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, and sliced green onions separate. Pat chicken dry, cut evenly, and refrigerate covered until the skillet is ready. Toss with the remaining 2 teaspoons cornstarch just before searing. Do not rinse chicken; wash hands and clean its preparation surfaces afterward.

When the rice has about 25 to 30 minutes left until serving, including the saucepan rest if used, put the broccoli and 1/4 cup water in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cover and steam for 3 to 4 minutes until bright green and just tender-crisp. Transfer to a bowl and carefully drain any remaining water; dry the skillet. The broccoli will finish in the sauce.

For stainless steel, preheat the dry skillet over medium heat, then add 2 teaspoons canola oil and swirl to coat. When shimmering, not smoking, spread half the chicken in one layer with gaps. Leave undisturbed for about 2 to 3 minutes, then gently test a piece; if stuck and not burning, give it another 30 seconds rather than tearing off the coating. Turn and cook about 3 to 5 minutes more, until lightly golden and the thickest pieces reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with another 2 teaspoons oil and the remaining chicken. Maintain a steady sizzle, lowering the heat if the coating or pan residue darkens too quickly; avoid maximum heat or induction boost. For nonstick, heat the oil with the pan following its maker's guidance. Do not crowd the pan or keep cooking done chicken for a darker crust.

Reduce heat to medium-low; on a heat-retaining pan, briefly lift it off the burner if still very hot. Keep golden-brown residue for the sauce. If any residue is blackened, let the pan cool enough to clean it out safely before continuing. Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon canola oil, ginger, garlic, and green-onion whites, and stir for about 30 seconds without browning the garlic. Whisk the sauce again to lift settled starch, pour it in, and gently scrape up the browned bits. Adjust heat to a simmer and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and lightly thickened. Return the broccoli for 1 to 2 minutes until tender to your liking, then add the cooked chicken and its juices just long enough to coat and warm through. Loosen with water a tablespoon at a time if too thick; do not reduce to a sticky syrup.

Remove from heat and stir in the orange zest, toasted sesame oil, and green-onion tops. Divide the rice and chicken-broccoli mixture equally among four plates or shallow containers. Serve immediately, or begin rapid cooling for meal prep as described in the notes.
notes: Allow about 60 to 65 minutes with saucepan brown rice and about 25 to 30 minutes of hands-on work. With the NP-HCC10 BROWN cycle, plan about 95 to 105 minutes from measuring rice to serving; use the final 25 to 30 minutes for the skillet cooking, adjusting to the cooker's countdown. Its longer hands-off cycle does not make the skillet method faster. Plain quick-cooking brown rice can shorten dinner to about 30 to 35 minutes: use enough dry rice to yield roughly 3 cups cooked and follow its package saucepan directions, not the regular BROWN cycle.

Rice cooker option, including Zojirushi NP-HCC10/XH: Start the rice before the other cooking. For Lundberg brown basmati, rinse and drain the recipe's 1 standard US cup of dry rice and add 1 3/4 standard US cups water, following the rice producer's rice-cooker ratio. Use BROWN, not QUICK or WHITE; follow a different rice brand's rice-cooker water guidance when supplied. Measure both amounts with standard US cups, not the supplied 180 mL rice cup. Zojirushi's BROWN water lines are for short-/medium-grain brown rice measured with its supplied cup, so do not top up to those lines as well. Allow about 84 to 90 minutes for the regular BROWN cycle, with variation by conditions; the cycle includes soaking and steaming, so fluff when it finishes without adding the saucepan's 10-minute rest. GABA BROWN takes much longer. Keep chicken, sauces, and vegetables out of the rice cooker.

Rice-cooker serving and meal prep: Use the supplied nonmetal rice paddle. If dinner needs a short delay, hold only plain cooked rice on the powered REGULAR KEEP WARM setting according to the manual, not in a switched-off cooker. For meal prep, move rice to shallow containers and begin the rapid cooling and freezing plan in these notes; KEEP WARM is not a way to reheat refrigerated or frozen rice.

Sweet orange juice supplies most of the sweetness; zest and toasted sesame oil go in off heat for a fresher finish. Measure the honey rather than using a sweet bottled orange sauce. Use unseasoned vinegar and reduced-sodium soy sauce; no extra salt, stock, hoisin, or soy drizzle is included. Reduced-sodium soy sauce still contains substantial sodium. This recipe contains soy and sesame, and usually wheat from soy sauce.

The light cornstarch coating helps the sauce cling; this is not a breaded or crispy fried dish. Stir the sauce just before adding because cornstarch settles. Batch-sear the chicken and briefly finish it in the sauce to avoid drying it out. For eight servings, cook the skillet portion in separate batches.

Meal prep with rice: Use the conservative UK Food Standards Agency plan of refrigerating only portions to be eaten within 24 hours and freezing the rest. Divide rice into shallow portions as soon as the cooking cycle or saucepan rest is complete and cool rapidly, ideally within 1 hour of cooking; a cold-water bath around a shallow metal container can help. Do not leave rice in the pot to cool. Refrigerate or freeze promptly, with the refrigerator at 40 degrees F or below and freezer at 0 degrees F or below. Refrigerate other cooked food within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90 degrees F.

Pack rice beside the sauced chicken and broccoli, label the date, and aim to use frozen meals within 2 months for quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and use within 24 hours of thawing. Reheat rice only once and eat promptly; reheating does not make poorly stored rice safe. For meal prep, cook a fresh batch of rice rather than reheating frozen rice, chilling it again, and reheating it later.

Reheating: Thaw one frozen portion overnight in the refrigerator. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons water, cover with a microwave-safe vented lid, and heat at medium to medium-high power in 60-second intervals, stirring or turning between intervals. Use shorter intervals near the end. After a 1-minute stand, check several spots with a thermometer and continue until all hot components reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Reheat only the portion being eaten and serve promptly. Add the water mainly to the rice; the sauce will loosen when stirred. Frozen broccoli will be softer, not crisp, after reheating.

Frozen broccoli works by equal weight. Cook according to its package, drain well, and add when the sauce is thickened instead of using the fresh-broccoli steaming step. Excess thawed water dilutes the sauce. Avoid seasoned bags and keep the measured oil and soy sauce unchanged.

Prep tools: For this batch, use a fine grater for ginger and orange zest, a knife for garlic, green onions, and broccoli, and a whisk for the sauce. A large food processor is not needed for the small sauce; chopping the broccoli in it would lose the florets. The stainless-steel method keeps the original measured oil, soy sauce, and cornstarch amounts; adding oil or salty sauce to compensate for sticking is not part of the method.
title: Orange-Ginger Chicken with Broccoli and Brown Rice
